---作文题目---
Write an essay of 150-200 words. Explain how a campus library can support independent learning.
---学生作文---
A campus library is more than a place where students borrow books. It is also a place where they can build habits that help them study without constant instruction. For this reason, universities should treat the library as an important part of daily learning.

The library provide a quiet room for students who cannot concentrate in a crowded dormitory. Students can studies there after class and compare several sources before forming an opinion. When they meet an unfamiliar term, a librarian can show them how to search for reliable information instead of giving them a ready answer.

The library provide workshops as well. A short session about planning a research project can help beginners divide a large task into manageable steps. However, workshops should remain optional, since students have different schedules and levels of experience.

To make these services useful, the university should ask students what they need and publish clear opening hours. With suitable support and enough freedom to choose their own methods, students can gradually become more responsible for their learning.
---数据结束---

---作文题目---
Write an essay of 150-200 words. Discuss one benefit and one limitation of group study.
---学生作文---
Group study can be useful when students are learning a difficult subject. A group gives them a chance to explain ideas aloud and notice gaps in their understanding. However, simply sitting at the same table does not guarantee that everyone will learn.

In a well organised session, each member prepares a question before the meeting. Each student have time to describe a problem, while the others listen and ask for clarification. Explaining a solution can make a concept more easier to remember because the speaker has to connect the separate steps.

There are also limits. One confident member may answer every question, leaving quieter students with little opportunity to think. A meeting can become a social conversation if the group has no clear goal. These problems are especially serious when an examination is close and study time is limited.

I would therefore combine group sessions with individual practice. Members could agree on a short agenda, take turns leading the discussion and finish by solving a new problem alone. This approach keeps the benefits of cooperation while allowing each student to check personal progress.
---数据结束---

---作文题目---
Write an essay of 150-200 words. Discuss how students should use online feedback.
---学生作文---
Online feedback has become a common part of university study. Students can receive comments on a draft before the next class, and teachers can respond to questions that would otherwise remain unanswered. These opportunities are valuable, but the usefulness of feedback depends of how it is interpreted.

A short response can give a useful informations about a specific sentence or calculation. It cannot always explain why the student made the mistake. If learners copy a suggested answer without considering the reason behind it, they may repeat the same problem in another task.

Students should therefore compare a comment with the original question, identify the part that needs attention and try to produce a new answer in their own words. When a suggestion seems unclear or conflicts with course materials, asking the teacher is more useful than guessing what was intended.

Teachers also have a role. Clear comments and a small number of priorities can help students focus their effort. In my view, online feedback works best as the beginning of a conversation, followed by revision and independent practice, rather than as a final judgement of ability.
---数据结束---

---作文题目---
Write an essay of 150-200 words. Discuss how universities can balance quiet study and social activity.
---学生作文---
A university needs spaces for both quiet concentration and informal conversation. Students do not all work in the same way, and their needs can change during the day. A successful campus should recognise these differences instead of expecting one room to serve every purpose.

Quiet study areas allow students to read demanding material, prepare for examinations and work without interruption. Social spaces support discussion and help new students form friendships. When these activities share a poorly planned area, ordinary conversation may disturb readers while requests for silence discourage useful exchange.

One practical solution is to separate spaces by purpose and make the rules visible. A library could reserve some floors for silent work while offering rooms where small groups can discuss a project. Students should also have a way to report problems and suggest improvements, since a rule that looks sensible on paper may be inconvenient in practice.

The aim is to provide reliable choices. By reviewing how rooms are used and listening to different groups, a university can protect concentration without treating social activity as a nuisance. Both forms of campus life deserve thoughtful support.
---数据结束---

[1] A student research group at a fictional college wanted to understand how its classmates used a newly renovated reading room. For eight weeks, volunteers recorded how often they visited the room and how long they stayed. Participation was optional, and the group made clear that the project would not affect anyone's grades.

[2] At the end of the period, the volunteers also reported the marks they had received in one course. Students who visited the reading room more often tended to report higher marks. The researchers initially found the pattern encouraging, since the room had been designed to support study. However, their supervisor asked them to consider other possible explanations before making a recommendation.

[3] Students chose for themselves whether to visit the room. Those with stronger study habits might have used it more often, and students taking different courses might have faced different assessments. The group had not measured these differences at the start. It had also relied on volunteers to report their own visits and marks, which introduced another source of uncertainty.

[4] The final report presented the association but did not claim that the room caused better academic performance. It recommended a larger study that would collect information about previous attainment and study habits. A comparison with students who used other places might also help, provided their circumstances were considered carefully.

[5] The college still regarded the room as a useful facility. Students described it as comfortable, and demand for its seats remained high. Yet the report separated these observations from the question of academic effects. A popular service can have practical value even when a particular causal claim has not been established. The researchers therefore suggested improving the room in response to users' comments while continuing to investigate its possible educational benefits.
---本篇题目与学生作答---
第 1 题：Which conclusion is justified by the study as described?
A. Using the room necessarily raises every student's marks
B. Higher marks prevent students from visiting the room
C. Visits and marks were associated, but the cause remained uncertain
D. The room had no practical value for any student

---篇章 1（段落已编号）---
[1] A fictional university archive collected interviews with former students for an exhibition about campus life. The project team wanted the interviews to be useful for future researchers as well as for visitors to the exhibition. Before recording began, participants received a form explaining how their contributions could be stored and displayed.

[2] Participants could choose between two levels of access. Some agreed that their recordings could be made available to the public. Others allowed researchers to consult the recordings in the archive but did not permit publication online. The team kept these choices with each recording so that staff would not have to rely on memory when responding to a request.

[3] The exhibition included only extracts that met the participants' stated conditions. A short extract still required permission for public use; removing most of a recording did not remove that requirement. The team also checked names and dates with the speakers where possible. When an account remained uncertain, the exhibition described it as a personal recollection rather than a confirmed institutional fact.

[4] After the exhibition closed, the archive kept the recordings under the original access conditions. Closing the exhibition did not automatically make restricted interviews public. Researchers who wanted to quote from a recording had to follow the relevant permission process, even if they had already listened to it in the reading room.

[5] The archive later reviewed its cataloguing system to make these restrictions easier to understand. Staff suggested adding clearer notes and training volunteers to explain the difference between consultation and publication. The aim was to improve access without making promises that the participants had never agreed to. The project showed that preserving an interview and making it freely available are separate decisions, each requiring careful records and clear communication.

第 1 题：What principle guided the archive after the exhibition?
A. Every preserved recording had to become freely available online
B. Listening in the archive automatically allowed online publication
C. Closing the exhibition removed all earlier restrictions
D. Access and publication continued to follow the participants' permissions
学生所选：A
